title: trio-sdk-auth-bridge: coordinated token migration, stream presets and ergonomic surface
author: Ava Martinez
description: Motivation: Several downstream apps reported awkward token migration when customers rotate credentials across services and observed subtle stream interruptions during credential refresh. This PR introduces a lightweight "trio" auth bridge and a small ergonomic surface that aligns refresh/backoff semantics across Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs while preserving backwards compatibility. Scope: coordinated changes across SDK facades (py/ts/go) and the monorepo bridge layer. Goals: 1) Provide a single opt-in mode (auth.bridgeMode = "trio") that triggers coordinated token handoff and staged refresh to avoid mid-stream token holes. 2) Standardize backoff presets and named streaming presets (low-latency, balanced, throughput) exposed from SDKs. 3) Keep public SDK APIs stable: new fields are optional and default to previous behavior. 4) Bump SDK minor versions to signal ergonomics additions. High-level change summary: - Add a minimal bridge shim in /internal/cred/bridge that exposes a consistent handshake and lease lifecycle. - Expose bridgeMode and streamPreset in each SDK config struct/class with typed enums and docs. - Normalize retry/backoff presets and wire them into streaming adapters (pullstream/pushstream) to reduce duplicated logic across languages. - Add small compatibility adapters to ensure legacy token callbacks continue to work (fallthrough path). Implementation notes: - Python: new redwood_sdk.session.auth.TrioBridge (thin wrapper), added stream_preset enum + integration tests against local canary harness. - TypeScript: introduced AuthBridge class in src/auth/bridge.ts and updated PullStreamAdapter to accept preset hints for buffering/heartbeat. - Go: lightweight credential fanout adapter in stream/connector/bridge.go with unit tests and integration test against perf-canary. - Telemetry: emit a single metric per SDK when bridgeMode switches (redwood.sdk.bridge.switch) and a streaming preset tag on request metrics. - Tests: added unit tests for each SDK; e2e run in perf-canary validated no increased median latency for small-burst streams. Rollout plan: - Feature gated: bridgeMode disabled by default. - Dogfood rollout on staging with several infra customers for one week. - Monitor telemetry for error spikes and token-mismatch counts. Checklist: - [x] Add thin bridge and adapters in all three SDKs - [x] Expose enums and types with docs - [x] Add unit + e2e tests in each repo - [x] Update changelogs and bump SDK minor versions - [x] Add telemetry and alert for token-mismatch regressions Related: ENG-2345 (migration playbook), PM-987 (product spec).

release_notes: SDKs: Introduce optional auth.bridgeMode="trio" to enable coordinated token handoff across Python/TS/Go SDKs. Add streamPreset hints (low-latency | balanced | throughput) to influence streaming adapter buffering and heartbeat heuristics. Backwards compatible; default behavior unchanged. Minor version bumps for SDKs.
notes_for_ops: Feature is gated. If you enable bridgeMode in production, monitor redwood.sdk.bridge.switch, redwood.sdk.token.mismatch_count and stream latency tags. Alert if token.mismatch_count > 5/min for a customer during rollout.
qa_summary: Unit tests added across languages (py/ts/go). CI initially flaked on a Go timeout test, extended test timeout in bridge_test.go and re-ran. Perf-canary e2e validates no regression on median latency for short-lived streams. Dogfood plan to run on staging for 7 days before broader enablement.
discussion_highlights: The team debated whether to make bridgeMode default-on; consensus was opt-in to avoid surprising customers. We prioritized a small ergonomic surface (enums + presets) rather than larger API surface changes. Telemetry tags were kept minimal to reduce cardinality.
post_merge_tasks: 1) Announce in #sdk-notify with migration notes and example config. 2) Coordinate with solutions for staging dogfood. 3) Follow up with a short runbook to handle token mismatch alerts.
extra_context: This PR is intentionally conservative: it standardizes patterns we've been iterating on for 6 months in per-SDK forks and pulls them into a single, minimal bridge implementation. The intent is to reduce duplicated token choreography and make future guarded rollouts (canarying bridge mode) straightforward.
